title: Creating a CollisionPolygon2D from a Sprite2D inherits scale from sprite (even though documentation advises never to scale collision polygons).
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in v4.2.1.stable.official [b09f793f5] and v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee] ### System information macOS 15.3.2 - Vulkan (Mobile) - integrated Apple M1 Pro - Apple M1 Pro (8 Threads) ### Issue description While using the tool in Sprite2D that allows you to create a CollisionPolygon2D I noticed a behaviour that I think is wrong. The Collision polygon that is created from the sprite inherits the scale of the sprite, it kinda makes sense because it also inherits the position, but I know the engine warns in multiple places about not scaling collision polygons because it creates erratic behaviour. I checked the Sprite2D tool (sprite_2d_editor_plugin.cpp) and noticed that it uses the method "clip_to_opaque_to_polygons" in "bit_map.cpp" and in there it's where the scale happens. As I said, I think it makes sense why it happens, probably that method is used in many instances but I think for the creation of collision polygons it should apply the scale to the nodes of the polygon and not to the scale of it. ### Steps to reproduce - Create a Sprite2D node in the hierarchy - Add an image to it - Modify the scale of the Sprite2D node - Select the Sprite2D node - Use the "Create CollisionPolygon2D Sibling" under the Sprite2D tool menu in the toolbar - Press "Create CollisionPolygon2D" in the preview window - Select the new CollisionPolygon2D in the hierarchy - Notice that the scale of it is the same as the Sprite2D node ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [collision2dissue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21376495/collision2dissue.zip)
